questions.question: What is the best first step in contraception counseling?
choices: Select the most common method before asking questions
Discuss pregnancy goals, preferences, medical history, medications, and safety context
Assume every patient wants a daily pill
Avoid asking about bleeding preferences
questions.explanation: Patient-centered contraceptive care begins with reproductive goals, preferences, medical eligibility, medication review, and safety assessment.

questions.question: What should be evaluated before starting or refilling combined hormonal contraception?
choices: Blood pressure and relevant cardiovascular/thrombotic risk factors
Only the patient’s preferred brand
Hair texture
Whether the patient has used a multivitamin
questions.explanation: Blood pressure and cardiovascular/thrombotic risk context are essential when assessing safety of estrogen-containing combined hormonal contraception.

questions.question: Why is a history of migraine aura important during combined hormonal contraception assessment?
choices: Aura never changes medication decisions
Migraine type and additional stroke-risk factors can change the safety of estrogen-containing methods
It confirms that every headache is benign
It eliminates the need to check blood pressure
questions.explanation: Accurate migraine classification, including aura, is important because it can alter combined hormonal contraceptive eligibility in the context of stroke risk.

questions.question: Which statement about long-acting reversible contraception is most appropriate?
choices: It should be required for patients who forget pills
It may reduce adherence burden but must be offered through informed, voluntary choice
It protects against all STIs
It never causes bleeding changes
questions.explanation: LARC can be highly effective and convenient, but patient autonomy, counseling, and individual suitability remain essential.

questions.question: Why is medication reconciliation important for hormonal contraception?
choices: Some medications can alter contraceptive effectiveness or safety
Only antibiotics ever interact with contraception
Medication changes do not affect pregnancy risk
It replaces pregnancy testing when indicated
questions.explanation: Some medications, including certain enzyme-inducing antiseizure medicines, can affect hormonal-contraceptive effectiveness. Current interaction resources should be checked.

questions.question: A patient has heavy vaginal bleeding, dizziness, severe pelvic pain, and possible pregnancy. What is the priority?
choices: Routine follow-up in six months
Urgent evaluation for instability and pregnancy-related causes
Automatic treatment as routine breakthrough bleeding
A menopause medication refill
questions.explanation: Heavy bleeding with dizziness, severe pain, and pregnancy concern may represent an urgent condition and requires timely evaluation.

questions.question: What is the safest general response to a positive pregnancy test in a patient taking chronic medication?
choices: Stop every medication immediately
Review current labeling and untreated-disease risk, then coordinate an individualized plan
Ignore pregnancy status until the next refill
Use outdated pregnancy letter categories alone
questions.explanation: Pregnancy medication decisions require individualized risk-benefit review. Abrupt discontinuation of some chronic therapies can be harmful.

questions.question: Which bleeding pattern should not be dismissed as a routine menopausal change?
choices: Bleeding after menopause
A predictable menstrual period in adolescence
Mild cramps with a known cycle
A resolved spotting episode after a missed pill without other symptoms
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding needs evaluation for an underlying cause and should not be assumed to be a normal aging change.

questions.question: Which principle best describes menopausal hormone therapy?
choices: It is a universal anti-aging treatment
It is individualized by symptom target, risk, route, medical history, and follow-up
It never requires discussion of bleeding
It is appropriate without medication review
questions.explanation: Menopausal symptom therapy requires individualized risk-benefit assessment, counseling, and reassessment rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

questions.question: What should be included in follow-up after starting a reproductive-health medication?
choices: Only whether the prescription was filled
Efficacy, adverse effects, bleeding pattern, warning symptoms, blood pressure when relevant, and patient satisfaction
No follow-up if the patient is younger than 40
A decision based only on a friend’s experience
questions.explanation: Effective follow-up evaluates benefit, safety, bleeding, relevant vital signs, warning symptoms, and whether the method remains aligned with the patient’s goals.
